# A need with a cap

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`a-need-with-a-cap` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](a-need-with-a-cap.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where a need has a cap, levels keep a formation within its band between need and cap; with balance the band is exact on both sides, a part opening it from below by giving and closing it from above by giving beyond the margin to the cap.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Levels keep a formation within its band at a step where each condition it requires stands between its need and its cap; levels within the band admit it. (`Becoming.Web.FitsBand`, `Becoming.Web.FitsBand.admits`)
2. With balance at the conditions required across the steps before, the levels that stand keep the formation within its band exactly where, at each, need plus what the part took is at most the level without the part plus what it gave, which is at most the cap plus what it took. (`Becoming.Flow.fitsBand_iff_within_margins_at`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; balance at the conditions the formation requires, across the steps before; whole-number levels.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Which needs have caps in an actual world.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
